sentences.text:
1  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER  SECTION 173(1) OF M.V. ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND  AWARD DATED: 28.02.2015, PASSED IN M.V.C. NO.140/2013 ON  THE FILE OF THE MEMBER, ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS  TRIBUNAL, HONAVAR, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR  COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL, COMING ON FOR  ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:3832  MFA No. 102709 of 2016  JUDGMENT
Though the matter is listed for admission, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. Heard Sri.T.M.Nadaf, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri.G.N.Raichur, learned counsel for respondent No.1.
3.
Claimant is in appeal, challenging the validity of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.140/2013 dated 28.02.2015 on the file of Additional MACT, Honavar.

4. Briefs facts of the case are as under:
A claim petition came to be filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act contending that claimant sustained accidental injuries on 27.03.2013 at about 9.15 a.m. near Kamat Hotel, Honnavar, on account of rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing No.KA.47/J- 4134.
5. Charge sheet came to be filed against the rider of the motorcycle.

Tribunal, on contest, allowed the claim petition in a sum of Rs.1,67,840/- as under:
7.
Being aggrieved by the same, claimant is in appeal.

8. Sri.T.M.Nadaf, learned counsel vehemently contended that Tribunal has grossly erred in taking the disability factor as 6% and it should have been at least 9%, in view of the fact that P.W.2 is not a treated doctor.

Vasudev S/O Devaray Deshbhandari vs Dinesh Shivayya Ambig on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142852071/
2 9.

He also contended that Tribunal has taken monthly income in a sum of Rs.5,000/- and claimant has stated Rs.6,000/- and in the absence of proper proof of income, Tribunal would normally assess sum of Rs.7,000/- as the monthly income for the accidental injuries sustained in the year 2013 and sought for enhanced compensation.
10. He further pointed out that Tribunal has not granted any amount of compensation on head of loss of amenities and sought for allowing the appeal.

11. Per contra, Sri.G.N.Raichur, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company, supported the impugned judgment contending that all the NC: 2024:KHC-D:3832 fractures are united and therefore, there is no disability involved in the incident and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

12. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record,
meticulously.

13. On such perusal of the material on record, the fact of the accidental injuries sustained by the claimant in a road traffic accident as aforesaid stands established by placing necessary oral and documentary evidence on record.
Wound certificate shows that there are multiple fractures.
14. Though all the fractures are united, there would be some amount of disability on account of accidental injuries sustained by the claimant.
Therefore, Tribunal ought to have taken 9% disability factor as against 25% assessed by the doctor, who is not a doctor, who treated the claimant and only issued disability certificate.

15. As rightly contended by Sri.T.M. Nadaf, learned counsel, monthly income should have been assessed and at least Rs.6,000/- in view of the fact that claimant has NC: 2024:KHC-D:3832 claimed Rs.6,000/- and Tribunal has taken Rs.5,000/-.

Instead of enhancing the compensation on each and every head, enhancing the compensation in a sum of Rs.50,000/- would meet the ends of justice.
16.

Accordingly, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed as against sum of Rs.1,67,840/-, claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.2,17,840/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
ii. Insurance Company is granted four weeks' time to pay the balance amount.
